call_points.text: FY27 volume growth guided at high teen, with EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26 and potential for improvement.
Order book split: industrial about 40%, passenger cars 25-30%, commercial vehicles 25-30%, rest off-highway and farm.
OEM price revisions: about 30% of the benefit came in Q1, full impact from Q2; increases are on a base last settled three years back.
Utilisation at 59% for forging and 78% for machining in Q1FY27.
Captive solar project expected on stream from January, with some generation from Q4; benefit of 1-1.5% on margins.
Capex of ₹350-400 Cr a year to be funded from own accruals, with only a possible bridge loan for letters of credit.
Management is open to acquisitions or JVs in energy and aerospace for technology and approvals, but cautious on farm and CV where valuations are expensive.
Europe accounts for about 60% of exports; inquiry flow from European OEMs is strong.
Next two years' planned capex is ₹800 Cr, including the solar plant.
About ₹140 Cr of new business won in the last quarter and four months, largely industrials and passenger vehicles.
Steel is a pass-through with a one-month domestic and one-quarter export lag; management seeks 3.5-4% price increases for other costs.
Machining capacity to rise from 69,000 to 82,000 tons by FY27 and 87,000 tons by FY28.

operating_notes.text: New-business order book of ₹950 Cr carries realisation of ₹345-350/kg versus current average of ₹245/kg, a gap of about ₹90-95/kg.
FY26 finished goods volume grew 10.9% and Q4 volume 20.6%, with realisation stable at about ₹245/kg despite a 6% fall in raw material prices.
Q4 domestic CV grew about 27% and PV about 35%, while CV exports fell about 25% and domestic off-highway fell 6%.
Finished goods volumes rose 23.1% and realisation per kg improved 3.2% to ₹253 in Q1FY27.
Order book of ₹950 Cr peak incremental annual revenue over two to three years, about 60% exports, led by industrial and passenger vehicle programs.
Europe accounts for about 60% of exports; container freight cost rose from USD 2,000 to USD 6,000 with about 75% pass-through.

timeline.summary: On its 22 May 2026 Q4FY26 earnings call, Happy Forgings guided FY27 volume growth at late teens with EBITDA margins near FY26's 30.4%, flagged a ₹950 Cr new-business order book and ₹450-500 Cr FY27 capex.
On 5 August 2026 Happy Forgings' Q1FY27 call reported revenue of ₹449 Cr (+27% YoY), EBITDA margin of 31.3% and PAT of ₹91 Cr, with a ₹950 Cr order book and high-teen FY27 volume growth guidance.

watchlist.response: Management declined to give a specific number, saying only that gross margin and EBITDA margin should improve with the higher-realisation order book.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for FY28 volume growth and margin targets

watchlist.response: Management said infrastructure must be in place first, expects most infra ready by Q4, but a 6-9 month development lead time follows; no acceleration committed.
watchlist.text: Analyst pressed on fast-tracking data-centre capex given Q3FY28 revenue start looks late

watchlist.response: Gave percentage ranges by end-user segment and a 60:40 export-domestic split, without rupee figures per segment.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for a segment-wise breakup of the ₹950 Cr order book; management gave only broad ranges (industrial ~40%, PV 25-30%, CV 25-30%).

watchlist.response: Management attributed margins to complex, high-realisation products and price increases on a base last settled three years back, and said it is confident of upwards of 30%.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked whether high gross and EBITDA margins could come down versus peers.

watchlist.response: About 75% pass-through; expects a 15-20% hit on incremental cost and hopes to recover about USD 4,500 of the USD 6,000 cost from customers.
